Fifth, new Rule 3(ca) requires intermediaries offering SGI-creation tools to additionally inform users that directing their computer resource to create unlawful SGI in contravention of new sub-rule 3(3) may attract penalties under the Act, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, POCSO Act 2012, Representation of the People Act 1951, Indecent Representation of Women Act 1986, Sexual Harassment at Workplace Act 2013, and Immoral Traffic Prevention Act 1956; and that such contravention may lead to immediate content removal, account suspension without vitiating evidence, identity disclosure to victims in accordance with applicable law, and mandatory crime reporting to the appropriate authority. New Rule 3(cb) requires intermediaries to take expeditious and appropriate action upon becoming aware of any SGI violation under sub-rule 3(3), including the consequences specified in Rule 3(ca)(ii). Sixth, the flagship new provision is Rule 3(3), imposing due diligence obligations on any intermediary that offers a computer resource enabling, permitting or facilitating the creation, generation, modification, alteration, publication, transmission, sharing or dissemination of information as SGI. Such intermediary must: (a)(i) deploy reasonable and appropriate technical measures including automated tools or other suitable mechanisms to prevent users from creating any SGI that violates any law, expressly including SGI containing child sexual exploitative and abuse material (CSAM), non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), obscene or sexually explicit content, false documents or false electronic records, instructions for explosive materials or arms or ammunition, or content that falsely depicts or portrays a natural person or real-world event in a deceptive manner; and (a)(ii) ensure that all SGI not covered under sub-clause (i) — that is, lawfully created synthetic content — is prominently labelled with a label that is easily noticeable and adequately perceivable in visual display, or through a prominently prefixed audio disclosure in the case of audio content, identifying it as AI-generated; and is embedded with permanent metadata or other appropriate technical provenance mechanisms including a unique identifier to identify the computer resource used to create it; and (b) not enable the modification, suppression or removal of the label, permanent metadata or unique identifier. Seventh, new Rule 4(1A) imposes additional obligations on Significant Social Media Intermediaries (SSMIs): before permitting any user to display, upload or publish information, SSMIs must require users to declare whether the content is SGI; deploy appropriate technical measures including automated tools to verify the accuracy of such declarations having regard to the nature, format and source of the information; and where declaration or technical verification confirms the content is SGI, ensure it is clearly and prominently labelled. SSMIs that knowingly permit, promote or fail to act on unlawful SGI are deemed to have failed due diligence. Rule 4(4) is strengthened from an aspirational 'endeavour to deploy' to a mandatory obligation to 'deploy appropriate technical measures including automated tools or other suitable mechanisms' for proactive identification of CSAM and previously-removed content. Timeframe changes across the rules: unlawful content removal window under Rule 3(1)(d) shortened from 36 hours to 3 hours on receipt of actual knowledge; NCII/morphed image removal window under Rule 3(2)(b) shortened from 24 hours to 2 hours; general grievance resolution window under Rule 3(2)(a)(i) shortened from 15 days to 7 days; certain content removal requests (all categories under Rule 3(1)(b) except sub-clauses (i), (iv), (xi)) shortened from 72 hours to 36 hours. Authorised officer provisions for content removal orders are strengthened: police administration may now have multiple DIG-rank authorised officers (previously only one); all removal intimations are subject to monthly review by a Secretary-rank officer for necessity, proportionality, and consistency with Section 79(3)(b) IT Act. The Indian Penal Code reference in Rule 7 is replaced with Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.
who_it_applies_to: All intermediaries operating in India as defined under Section 2(w) of IT Act 2000; Significant Social Media Intermediaries (SSMIs) notified above the user threshold; online gaming intermediaries; publishers of news and current affairs content; publishers of online curated content (OTT platforms); any intermediary that offers a computer resource enabling the creation, generation, modification, alteration, publication, transmission, sharing or dissemination of information as synthetically generated information (including GenAI tool providers, AI image/video/audio generation platforms, deepfake-capable applications, social media platforms with AI creation features, and any platform providing synthetic content functionality to Indian users)
key_obligations: [All intermediaries] Publish rules, privacy policy, user agreement in user's preferred Eighth Schedule language; periodically inform users at least once every three months of non-compliance consequences and applicable penalties and mandatory crime reporting obligations; acknowledge user grievances within 24 hours and resolve within 7 days (shortened from 15); remove NCII or morphed image content within 2 hours (shortened from 24) of complaint; remove unlawful content under Rule 3(1)(d) within 3 hours (shortened from 36) of actual knowledge via court order or authorised officer intimation; preserve removed content 180 days; respond to government information requests within 72 hours (24 hours for permissible online real money game intermediaries); report cyber security incidents to CERT-In; [Intermediaries offering SGI creation tools — Rule 3(3)] deploy reasonable and appropriate technical measures including automated tools to prevent creation of unlawful SGI (CSAM, NCII, obscenity, false documents, explosives/arms instructions, false depictions of real persons or events); ensure all permissible SGI is prominently labelled as AI-generated with visible label or audio disclosure; embed permanent metadata and unique identifiers in all SGI for provenance; prohibit suppression or removal of SGI labels or identifiers; additionally inform users of penalties and consequences for unlawful SGI creation including content removal, account suspension, identity disclosure to victims, and mandatory crime reporting; take expeditious action on becoming aware of SGI violations; [SSMIs — Rule 4(1A)] require user declaration before publication whether content is SGI; deploy technical verification of declarations; display prominent SGI labels on all confirmed synthetic content; [SSMIs — Rule 4(4)] deploy (not merely endeavour to deploy) appropriate technical measures for proactive identification of CSAM and previously-removed content with human oversight and periodic review; appoint India-resident Chief Compliance Officer, Nodal Contact Person, Resident Grievance Officer; publish monthly compliance reports; enable first originator traceability on court or Section 69 order; implement pre-removal notification for own-initiative content removal
